design_rationale:
WORKLOG task 0 (utility_pass_through_billing) — draw: draw_counts.py --task 0 -> prerequisite_problems=2, factor_counts=[4, 6, 5]; estimated read took 5, usage charge 4, final-statement prepayment 6.

WHY A GOOD TEST. A departing resident (Raymond T. Gaitan, Bluebonnet Ridge C-246) asks only to pay off his water account and prepay his last bill before his home is hauled away on 2026-10-09. The prepayment rule waits on a state the records lack: 'The prepayment of an estimated final statement is worked out only after a water usage charge stands on the account for every read cycle whose read day has passed.' The ledger shows the 2026-10-01 statement (fixed charges 9.85/38.50/21.75 and admin 3.25, 31 days) but no 2026-10 read and no 2026-10 usage charge. The usage-charge rule in turn waits: 'A water usage charge for a read cycle is fixed only after a water read stands on the account for that cycle's read day.' Only the estimated-read policy writes a read. So the agent must discover a 3-problem chain from the documents, record an estimate (5 factors), price it (4 factors), then quote and hand over the prepayment (6 factors). Difficulty comes from reading the policies and the ledger and from arithmetic, never from tool choice: each policy names one tool.

SCOPE. Task 0 claims utility_ext_estimated_water_read, utility_ext_water_usage_charge, utility_ext_final_statement_prepayment and tools post_estimated_water_read_4835faa0, post_water_usage_charge_d31cd699, prepay_final_statement_ca2cf476. Remaining for task 1 (draw: 1 prerequisite, factors [5, 5]): utility_ext_statement_late_fee (post_late_fee_5fe5b1d1) and utility_ext_final_credit_refund (request_credit_refund_3a7a9c57), a move-out refund tree with its own late-fee prerequisite. Leak adjustments and other adjustment credits were not claimed: every adjustment-credit write inherits the repair_proof caller-statement gate, whose correlation key is the account uuid and could only be satisfied by a persona reciting an internal id.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Root utility_ext_final_statement_prepayment (owner=user, on_request) <- utility_ext_water_usage_charge (agent, state_due; edge value_input, gate balance, state form, sentence above; false at opening: no 2026-10 usage charge, balance 73.35) <- utility_ext_estimated_water_read (agent, state_due; edge value_input, gate billed_kgal, state form; false at opening: latest water read 2026-08-22 is billed on 2026-09). Four-point test: both sentences carry 'only after', name a record-visible state (a usage charge standing for every passed read cycle; a water read standing for the cycle's read day), name no tool/id/code token, and are hard requirements scoped to read cycles. Exactly one write of the difficulty books a water usage charge (post_water_usage_charge_d31cd699) and exactly one records a water read (post_estimated_water_read_4835faa0). Topological order: estimate (step 11), usage charge (13), prepayment (15). Deletion sensitivity: skipping the usage charge gives prepayment 196.17 instead of 291.36; skipping the estimate gives usage charge 114.65 instead of 102.27. user_scenario mentions no prerequisite; tools validate none.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD. Estimated read (subject utility_meter_read): utility_evt_statement_billing and utility_evt_estimates_and_rereads carry no structured gate (policy_scope); the two-consecutive-estimate cap holds (2026-08-22 was actual). Usage charge (utility_usage_charge): utility_evt_statement_billing and utility_meter_accuracy (its only gate applies to meter tests) -> policy_scope; due date = statement 2026-10-01 + 20 = 2026-10-21. Prepayment (utility_payment): utility_agg_account_settlement (policy_scope) and utility_evt_payments, whose certified-funds clause is superseded by the prepayment rule's channel sentence (declared overwrite); the lease is not restricted (payment_restriction none) and a final-statement prepayment is accepted only by card through the portal or cashier's check. No time gate applies.

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. One utility account 7332db5e-2b1c-4393-a62c-2825e32a9fc6 (final_read_pending, service_end_date 2026-10-09). Target cycle: the read cycle 2026-08-22 -> 2026-09-22 billed on 2026-10. Rows aggregated: actual water reads (Oct 2025-Aug 2026, ten of them in twelve months), the 2026-02-22 estimate (counted only as an estimate), the 2026-08-10 leak credit, the latest usage charge, the October 1 fixed charges. Excluded: the 2025-09-22 read for the estimate basis (household changed), the June read for the three-month basis, the estimated reads for every average.

FACTOR CARD. Estimated read: basis method (lease occupant registration 2026-03-16 -> three-month average 23.00; baseline four-month 20.73), earlier-estimate share 0.93 (one estimate), guest share 1.25 (28-day stay), move-out share 0.85 (vacate in 8 days), leak share 0.80 (credit 2026-08-10); result 18.79, baseline_result 21.42. Usage charge: household share 0.75, guest widening 0.50, lot share 1.40, estimated-read pricing (first estimate: part above second bound at midpoint 6.71); result 102.27, baseline 119.42. Prepayment: twelve-month daily-use basis, move share 0.80, guest share 1.25, 15-29-day fixed proration, 20% cushion (returned lease payment 2026-05-04), 15% true-up reserve; result 291.36, baseline 312.92. Per-factor baseline results are in computations[].factor_sensitivity; each differs from gold. Cross-difficulty evidence: lease (occupants, lot class, notice, occupant registration, returned payment) and rules (guest registration). Multi-source: estimate basis (read a year earlier AND no household change / household change AND recent reads), move-out shares (notice AND vacate distance), cushion (lease return OR utility return).

WORLD. Twelve monthly cycles of reads, usage charges, three fixed charges, admin fee and portal-ACH payments, all priced under the extended pricing (household 2 before the 2026-03-16 registration, then 1; Greenbelt second bound 14.00); the February estimate follows the estimate rule at 2026-03-01 (8.44); the August leak credit follows the base leak formula (51.67). Lease: Greenbelt, twelve-month term ending 2026-10-09, notice accepted 2026-08-03 (67 days, above the 60-day minimum), one occupant; May 2026 rent payment returned for insufficient funds with the 35.00 NSF fee and a card replacement inside grace (one return: no certified-funds restriction). Rules: self-maintained site, guest Daniel R. Gaitan 2026-09-12 to 2026-10-10 (28 days, within the 30-day guest maximum, registered 2026-09-19 after 7 days).

PERSONA. Plain-spoken retiree; volunteers only the goal, the move date and that he pays himself in the portal; credentials on request; passive consent to any bookkeeping the agent explains; switches to his Visa debit card only if told a bank payment is not accepted; ends after reading back the confirmation number.

STANDARD SOLUTION. Locate/verify; read account, ledger, requests, lease, lease requests, lease ledger, rules plan and records; record estimate 18.79 kgal for 2026-10 dated 2026-09-22 from register 2000.56; post usage charge 102.27 due 2026-10-21 against the new read; quote 291.36 and hand over the prepayment, paid by online_portal_card.

VERIFICATION. Code (authoring script, deleted after use) replayed gold with the real tools and evaluated each compute through check_compute's DSL on the handling-time world: estimate 18.79, usage 102.27, prepayment 291.36; factor substitutions as listed. Gates run: check_extended, check_task_tools, replay_tasks, check_solvability, check_compute, check_grounding, check_cross_fire (--task 0).

DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM VISIBLE CONTEXT. From the prose rules alone: the prepayment rule's prerequisite sentence plus the ledger (no 2026-10 usage charge) points to the usage-charge rule, whose sentence plus the ledger (no 2026-10 read) points to the estimate rule; the estimate, charge and prepayment figures above follow from the published ladders, the lease, the rules records and the ledger with no hidden value. Revision log: lot share initially decorative under the first-estimate pricing (blocks two and three both at the second rate); the first-estimate method was changed to price only the part above the second bound at the midpoint rate, after which every factor moves its result.
user_scenario: You are Raymond T. Gaitan, seventy-one, a retired pipefitter and a widower who has lived on site C-246 at Bluebonnet Ridge in Conroe, Texas, for about twelve years. You are moving to your daughter's place in Tucson: a dealer bought your home and is hauling it off the site on October 9, and you already gave the community your written notice for that date months ago. You call the resident desk on the morning of October 1. What you want is simple and you say it plainly near the start: you want to pay off your water account today, everything you owe plus your last bill ahead of time, so nothing follows you to Arizona. You want it done on this call and you will make the payment yourself through the resident portal once the agent works out the amount and sets it up for you; you do not want the agent to charge anything on your behalf, and you have no idea what the final bill will come to, so you never offer a figure of your own. You open by giving your phone number, 936-555-0131. Only when the agent asks you to verify do you give the last four of your Social Security number, 2218, and only if asked for your date of birth do you say February 11, 1955 (1955-02-11). You do not know any account or customer reference numbers. If the agent asks who is in the home, you say you live alone, but your son Daniel has been staying with you since September 12 to help you pack and will leave on October 10; the office has him registered as a guest. If the agent asks how you usually pay, you say you pay the water bill online from your checking account. If the agent says this payment can't come from your checking account and has to be a card or a cashier's check, you say that's fine, you'll use your Visa debit card in the portal today. If the agent explains that something on the account has to be put on the books first, such as a reading or a charge, you tell them to go ahead and do whatever has to be done; you don't ask what or why. When the agent sets the payment up for you and tells you the amount, you pay exactly that amount through the portal by the method the agent named, and you read back the confirmation number the portal gives you. Once you have that confirmation number you thank the agent and say goodbye; you don't bring up anything else.

base_preconditions.condition: Every submeter is read on the schedule's meter_read_day and consumption between consecutive reads is billed on the statement of the following month; no structured eligibility gate applies to recording a read.

When a submeter cannot be read on the read day the cycle is billed on an estimate; no more than two consecutive cycles may be estimated (the August cycle was an actual read, so this estimate is the first in a row).

gold_actions.business_effect: Posts the regular water usage charge of 102.27 on the October 1 statement for the estimated September 22 read, due October 21, raising the utility balance from 73.35 to 175.62.

request_binding.action_semantics: Once a read stands for the September 22 read day, the statement month 2026-10 has a read without its water usage charge; the usage-charge policy owes that charge. Only the usage-charge action bills a read; the estimate itself books nothing on the balance.
